title: Pythagoras' theorem: a² + b² = c²
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class squares both legs before adding when finding a hypotenuse.
The class can name the hypotenuse reliably as the side across from the right angle.

modelAnswers.question: A right-angled triangle has legs 6 and 8. Find the hypotenuse, showing your working.
A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 13 and one leg 5. Find the other leg, showing your working.
modelAnswers.answer: The other leg squared is 13² - 5² = 169 - 25 = 144, so the other leg is 12.

commonErrors.example: A learner writes the tangent ratio with the adjacent side on top, flipping the two shorter sides.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: label the opposite and adjacent sides for theta first, then rewrite the tangent ratio by reading TOA aloud.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: TOA gives tan theta with opposite over adjacent, so the side across from theta belongs in the numerator of the ratio.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner defends the flipped tangent ratio by pointing at the side next to theta.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: swap the numerator and denominator of the flipped ratio and check the result against the 3-4-5 triangle on the notes card.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: for the 3-4-5 triangle the tangent value is the smaller-over-larger ratio of the two legs, matching opposite divided by adjacent.

nextSteps: Reteach TOA with side labelling before any ratio is written, using the 3-4-5 triangle as the anchor example.
Practise finding a missing leg by rearranging before returning to mixed hypotenuse questions.
